reasons: Classification is correct: § 12.4 is a one-way no-hire ('solicit, hire, or employ') covering any Vendor employee for 24 months post-term and expressly negating a general-advertising/unsolicited-approach carve-out ('regardless of how the employee applies'), which fails the fallback on every material term and sits in walk-away territory.

The redline reaches the fallback precisely: mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in performing or receiving the Services, 12 months from the end of that involvement, general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs added, and the 'hire, or employ' no-hire language deleted.

The failed minimal-edit heuristic (0.851 changed-character ratio) is acceptable here — the original clause was one-way, over-broad and anti-carve-out, so no smaller edit could reach the fallback; the rewrite adds nothing beyond what the rule requires.

Comment is accurate, correctly scoped, uses the required prefix and tone, and the cross-reference to § 12.3 (Vendor's acknowledgement that Customer gave no no-hire commitment) is supported by the cited text.
No double-flagging or counterparty-favourable over-reach: the drafted clause is mutual rather than one-sided in our favour, and the restriction does not exceed the playbook's accepted fallback.
